stem:
Rohit needs to separate fine besan from larger chickpea bits using a kitchen sieve. He also has a cup of salt water on the side.

Which choice is correct?

options.text: Use a sieve whose holes are larger than the fine besan but smaller than the chickpea bits, so the besan passes through and the bits remain on the sieve.
Use a sieve whose holes are larger than both the fine besan and the chickpea bits.
Use a sieve whose holes sit between their sizes so the fine besan remains on the sieve and the bigger chickpea bits pass through.
Use the sieve to remove dissolved salt from salt water.

teacher.key_rationale: Sieving separates by size when holes let the smaller particles through and hold the larger ones. Holes larger than both fail; swapping which size passes reverses the process; sieving does not remove dissolved salt.
